title: Reception in New Orleans, prejudice and music
summary: Albert drew crowds in New Orleans clubs but recalls prejudice there and in San Antonio, and says music and sports have fought it.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: You know, I've never understood, it brings me back to New Orleans, why somebody can be world famous and not make it in New Orleans, you know, musicians. It seems like they turn their back on me, this is off the subject.

Yeah, I never have been able to understand that myself. However, let me say this, that I have met up with a lot of great response when I had my band, when I came back to New Orleans, even though I was considered a Texas boy, by Texans and other people, but whenever I played here, the Santa Cendez was one of the places that I would just put thousands of people in. And also the old Tick Tock and the Pelican, we played those places by the time we tuned our horns up the line, was two blocks around to hit a Don Albert band.
Well, I'm not talking about the people, I just, it's funny, the attitude of night club owners and all that, I suspect, you know, that it's the same old race practice, it had something to do with it.

Well, in the past, it was so predominant here that a lot of times I dreaded coming back here. But now the trend is just a little bit different. But Dick, let me say this, that you're going to find this sort of people any way you go. When you're a Negro, you're just a Negro today. And times are not too much better, because I seem to want to be on the militant side, I have to be. I fought this thing and I fought prejudices in San Antonio, and I have letters from the governors, from the president, everyone else trying to get things for the Negroes settled right. But it's just a hatred, and I don't know what it is, within people that they just haven't been able to get rid of it. And until, until the day comes, when these things can be gotten out of a man's system, you're not going to have peace and harmony, nothing. It is known in the music, you find, of course it's predominant with you in the music because you follow this. But you can get in civil service such as I am and you'll find the same things that exist there.
It seems to me it's better in music than a lot of them. Yeah. A whole lot of people have been fighting racial prejudice for years, through music.
That's right, through music and sports. It's been the greatest medium.
